tagline: Your iPhone photos on your computer, over a cable.
state_no_device: Connect your iPhone with a USB cable
state_no_device_hint: Use a data cable (not charge-only), then unlock the iPhone.
state_not_paired_hint: The prompt shows on the iPhone. If you declined: unplug, plug back in.
driver_body_windows: Windows needs Apple's free 'Apple Devices' app to talk to the iPhone. Install it once from the Microsoft Store, then reconnect your iPhone.
driver_body_linux: Install it with your distribution's command, then reconnect the iPhone:
driver_body_other: Restart the computer, then reconnect the iPhone.
scan_summary: {total} files on the iPhone ({size}). {new} new to import ({newsize}).
format_unavailable_windows: JPG conversion is not available on Windows yet. Photos stay HEIC (the Photos app opens them).
format_unavailable_linux: To convert to JPG, install heif-convert: sudo apt install libheif-examples
delete_after_hint: Only files that were copied and verified.
delete_after_confirm: {n} imported and verified {n|file|files} will be permanently deleted from the iPhone. Continue?
layout_flat_ex: everything in the folder, no subfolders
grid_hint: Click to select, Shift+click for a range, drag to select an area. Double-click or ⤢ to preview.
search_placeholder: Search a place or a scene…
search_loading: Preparing search… (reading the iPhone's index, longer the first time)
preview_raw: RAW preview: the iPhone thumbnail is shown. The full RAW file will be imported.
preview_thumb_only: Full preview not available on this system: showing the thumbnail. The original will be imported.
preview_video_unsupported: This system cannot play this video here (often HEVC). It will still be imported intact.
scan_hint_first: PhotoPort is listing all your photos and videos. Thumbnails will show right after.
